component.name: Patchcord
component.summary: PipeWire patchbay drawn as a rack of gear

screenshot.caption: Devices on the desk, patched with cords
The same devices in a rack
ENGINE: PipeWire's real graph, with an app's details and timings

description.p: Patchcord shows your PipeWire audio and MIDI graph as a rack of hardware gear. Every device is a panel with 6.3 mm jacks, and every connection is a patch cord that hangs, swings and settles like a real one.

ul.li: Pull a cord from a jack and plug it into another to connect; pull it out to disconnect
Stereo jacks that split into separate left and right jacks
A signal meter in every input and output, and the state of each device
Plain names: SPEAKERS, HEADPHONES, MIC, from the port in use; what makes sound on the left, what takes it on the right
A light in each cord shows which way the sound goes
Each app's volume or recording gain, balance and mute, beside its jacks; an app with several streams gets a frame for each
Sound card volumes, ports (speakers or headphones) and latency offsets
The default output and input, chosen on the top panel
Listen to any jack, or in ENGINE any port (cue), in the default output, without repatching
Sound card profiles, such as Bluetooth hi-fi or headset and its codec
Devices on a desk, or in a 19" rack; hide the ones you don't use
Presets of connections, layouts, volumes and profiles, undo and redo
Hover a jack or cord for its full PipeWire names
ENGINE: PipeWire's real nodes, ports and links by the driver that clocks them, with timings, xruns, diagnostics and a report for bug tickets

description.p: MIXER, every device and app as a mixing console; links made in ENGINE; reports that keep the whole state.

ul.li: MIXER (M): every device and app as a module of a console, by what it does: faders, MUTE, CUE, where each app plays or records from, the defaults, a card's profile and port
DESK is now one of RACK's two views, on a switch in VIEW; a key a screen can't use is left off the panel
ENGINE links ports: drag from a port to another, or pick from a port's LINK FROM / LINK TO lists in its new CONN tab; undo works
SAVE REPORT keeps volumes, mute, cards' profiles and ports, still without your user and host names, MAC addresses or the titles of what plays
A sound card's frames are named so they can be told apart: a laptop's three HDMI outputs are HDMI 1, HDMI 2, HDMI 3, its microphones by their names
Video (a camera, a shared screen) is shown in ENGINE only, for now
Fixes: MIDI bridges shown as apps on newer PipeWire (1.6.11), names lost from reports

description.p: Listening that wakes nothing up and works in ENGINE too; ENGINE laid out by how things are linked.

ul.li: Listening (cue) has streams of its own: it no longer wakes sleeping devices or adds xruns, and LEVEL is remembered
In ENGINE, CUE mode: click a port to hear it, one channel in its own ear; the port a click would take is framed, and what is heard is filled cyan
In CUE mode a jack's hole still patches: pull a cord out, move it, plug a new one, and hear the result; the ring round it listens
A jack kept on fills its disc, half of it for one channel; a split pair gets one mark round both
ENGINE lays blocks out by their links: what only sends on the left, chains in the middle, what only takes on the right; no link runs through another's port, and blocks glide when the graph changes
ENGINE's tables and details scroll smoothly, with a scrollbar
Signal meters are left out for muted frames
Faster: cords no longer settle again on every frame while devices glide
Fixes: a crash some time after streams came and went, a touchpad running knobs to their end, lists opening off the bottom of the window, MAC addresses in pictures

description.p: ENGINE shows what PipeWire really has; and the app is faster, lighter and fits narrow windows.

ul.li: ENGINE (E): PipeWire's real nodes, ports and links, grouped by the driver that clocks them and coloured by what they are; click one for its details, its timing and where it is on the desk
A strip with the clock, quantum, DSP load, xruns and health, and diagnostics below: TOP as pw-top, ISSUES with what to do about them, OBJECTS, METADATA and EVENTS
SAVE REPORT writes all of it to a text file for a bug report, without your user and host names, MAC addresses or the titles of what plays
A legend (?) explains ENGINE's colours, lights, links and tags
Narrow windows: the top panel folds what doesn't fit into MORE, and ENGINE shows what matters most first
Faster: cords are drawn by the GPU, sharp at any zoom; pictures are drawn in the background, so zooming, dragging and switching screens no longer stall; the desk and the rack switch at once
Less memory: it is given back after big pictures
Signal meters show the signal itself, before the software volume
The hover and found glows are gone, and ALIGN is off in the rack, where it does nothing
PATCHCORD_FRAMES=1 prints slow frames and what took the time, for reports about speed

description.p: Easier to read: plain names, sound flowing left to right, and a light in the cords.

ul.li: A sound card's inputs and outputs are named by what they are, following the port in use: SPEAKERS, HEADPHONES, HDMI, BUILT-IN MIC, MIC
REC OUT, a copy of what an output plays, sits inside that output's frame
On every device what makes sound is on the left and what takes it on the right, so sound flows left to right
Every audio input and output has its own signal meter
FLOW: a light runs inside every cord from its output to its input
Hide devices you don't use with their HIDE key; the HIDDEN list shows them again, and what Patchcord always leaves out
Bigger apps spread over two or three units, balanced, with vents where a unit has nothing to show
A Bluetooth headset shows one MIC; WirePlumber's plumbing behind it is left out, as are apps' monitors
ARRANGE packs the desk to fit the window
Fixes: a face now redraws when its port changes (plugging in headphones)

description.p: A mixer on every device, and listening to any jack.

ul.li: VOLUME or GAIN, a push-push BAL knob and MUTE beside the jacks of each app stream and each device's output and input, as in pavucontrol
Sound cards: their hardware volume, a PORT list (speakers, headphones, microphones) with latency offsets, beside PROFILE
The default output and input on the top panel's screen, with a list to change them and find them on the desk
Cue: hold Alt over a jack to hear it in the default output, or turn on CUE mode to keep several playing, with its own LEVEL
An app with several streams (Teams, a browser's tabs) is one device with a numbered frame for each stream, each with its own controls and meter
At most three frames side by side: bigger devices grow to two or three units
Coloured bands by kind of group (K), meters in each frame, and a slimmer rack
Presets also keep volumes, profiles, ports and the defaults
The signal meters show both channels: sometimes only the left one moved, with an app's right channel measured as its left, when PipeWire changed a meter's ports while setting it up

description.p: A fix for patching, and an animation in the README.

ul.li: While a cord's end is in the hand, a jack already patched to its other end no longer glows as a place it fits: it takes no second cord, and the cord used to fall out there
The README shows Patchcord in use: cords patched, a device dragged into line, the rack and back

description.p: Lighter cords that hang like real ones, as in Reason; devices that line up and never lie over one another; and fixes for hovering, SPLIT and JOIN.

ul.li: Cords end straight in their jacks instead of in right-angle plugs: they simply hang between their jacks in smooth curves, with no loops, kinks or turning plugs
Cords hang in deep, calm curves like real cords, dropping out of their jacks; the SAG knob is gone
A cord pulled out of a jack comes out in a smooth curve, instead of a coil that unrolls
Cords follow their devices smoothly when they move, as when switching between desk and rack
When a cord is dropped, the jack its other end is still in keeps its place until the cord has gone
A split stereo jack shows its L jack above its R jack, both keeping the stereo jack's gold ring
SPLIT and JOIN carry over to every stereo jack patched to it, and on from there, so a stereo jack is never patched to a split one by two cords that each carry one channel

Devices on the desk line up: a dragged device's edges and centre stick lightly to those of the others, with a guide line, and it sits neatly right beside, above or below one; a button on the panel (G) turns this off to place devices freely

Devices on the desk never lie over one another: they can't be dragged over each other, they make room when one grows, and a device that comes back no longer lands on top of another one that took its place
JOIN on a split input jack joins the app output it is patched to as well, like JOIN on the output did
Hovering a jack, cord or device no longer makes the cords blink, and hovering one without cords leaves the others as they are
The live PipeWire graph as device panels with jacks, signal meters and state
Patch cords with physics, and right-angle plugs drawn to scale
Patching with the mouse: pull out, move and drop plugs; undo and redo
SPLIT and JOIN for stereo jacks, carried over to the jacks at the other end
Desk and rack layouts, presets, and settings kept as plain text files
The jacks a plug fits glow while it is in the hand; hover for tooltips
